The Brunei dollar is the official currency and the best choice. Some places might accept major foreign currencies, but Brunei dollars are generally more convenient and cost-effective. You can order Brunei dollars online with Manor FX today. Are USD accepted in Brunei? The Brunei dollar is the official currency, and transactions are typically done in this currency. However, US dollars are also widely accepted, especially in hotels, large retail outlets, and some restaurants catering to tourists. Tourist-oriented businesses commonly accept USD, but it’s always good to have some Brunei dollars on hand for smaller purchases, local markets, and places that might not accept foreign currencies. Remember, when paying in USD, the exchange rate might not always be in your favour, and change is usually given in Brunei dollars. Can I use the Brunei dollar in Singapore? Yes, the Brunei dollar and Singapore dollar are interchangeable at par. This unique agreement allows you to use Brunei dollars in Singapore just like the local currency and vice versa. Are credit cards accepted in Brunei? Yes, you can use your credit and bank cards in Brunei. However, it’s wise to have a mix of cash and cards. Smaller shops and local markets prefer cash, while larger stores and hotels usually accept cards. Tip: Inform your bank about travel plans to avoid card issues abroad. Should I use cash in Brunei? Though Brunei is gradually embracing cashless payments, cash is still valuable for smaller transactions. ATMs are widespread, making cash withdrawals easy. How much cash should I take to Brunei? Enjoying Brunei can be budget-friendly, whether you’re backpacking, seeking mid-range comfort, or indulging in luxury. Here’s a guide to managing your budget in this serene sultanate. Backpacking Brunei budgets Daily budget: Around 35 BND (£20). This could cover a hostel bed, local meals, public transport, and free sights like mosques and parks. Remember, hostels start from about 25 BND (£18), and meals can range from 7 to 15 BND. Mid-range budget Daily budget: Approximately 70-100 BND (£40-£60). Staying in comfortable hotels, eating out, enjoying a few drinks, taking taxis occasionally, and visiting paid attractions like museums could fit this budget. Luxury budget Daily budget: 150 BND (£85) and upwards. You’d need to budget generously for a luxurious experience that includes fine dining, taxis, top hotels, and any tours that catch your eye. Can I avoid ATM fees in Brunei? To save on ATM fees in Brunei: Check if your bank has partnerships with local banks for free withdrawals. Withdraw more significant sums less often to reduce transaction fees. Look for ATMs with lower fees. Do you tip in Brunei? Tipping isn’t customary in Brunei. Restaurant bills usually include service charges, so no extra tipping is required. Brunei keeps it simple: enjoy the service without the tipping fuss. Is Brunei expensive? Brunei can be considered relatively expensive compared to some other Southeast Asian countries, but this depends on your lifestyle and how you choose to spend your time and money. Accommodation, dining in restaurants, and specific activities can be pricier, similar to costs in Western countries. However, there are also ways to explore Brunei without spending a lot. Eating at local markets, using public transportation, and enjoying the country’s natural and cultural sights, many of which are free, can make your visit more affordable. Like any travel destination, careful planning and budget management can help you control costs and enjoy your visit to Brunei.
